# google_network_services_telemetry_policy

Provides a configuration for telemetry.


To get more information about TelemetryPolicy, see:
* How-to Guides
    * [api](https://cloud.google.com/network-services/docs/reference/network-services/rest/v1/projects.locations.telemetryPolicies)

## Example Usage - Network Services Telemetry Policy Basic


```hcl
resource "google_network_services_mesh" "default" {
  name     = "my-mesh"
}

resource "google_network_services_telemetry_policy" "default" {
  name     = "my-telemetry-policy"
  location = "global"

  telemetry_target {
    resources = [google_network_services_mesh.default.id]
  }

  labels = {
    foo = "bar"
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Network Services Telemetry Policy Full


```hcl
resource "google_network_services_mesh" "default" {
  name     = "my-mesh"
}

resource "google_network_services_telemetry_policy" "default" {
  name         = "my-telemetry-policy"
  location     = "global"
  display_name = "my-telemetry-policy"

  telemetry_target {
    resources = [google_network_services_mesh.default.id]
  }

  tracing_configuration {
    sampling_rate = 0.5
    custom_span_attributes {
      attribute_name = "attribute-name"
      literal_value  = "literal-value"
    }
    parent_based_sampling {
      enabled       = true
      sampling_rate = 0.5
    }
  }

  metrics_configuration {
    enabled = true
  }

  labels = {
    foo = "bar"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `telemetry_target` -
  (Required)
  Specifies the set of targets to which this telemetry policy applies.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_telemetry_target).

* `name` -
  (Required)
  Name of the TelemetryPolicy resource.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the telemetry policy.


* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  Set of label tags associated with the TelemetryPolicy resource.

  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  Provides a human-readable name for the policy.

* `tracing_configuration` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the top-level configuration block within the telemetry
  policy that contains all the settings for how tracing will be applied to
  the target resources.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_tracing_configuration).

* `metrics_configuration` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the top-level configuration block within the telemetry
  policy that contains all the settings for how metrics will be applied to
  the target resources.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_metrics_configuration).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_telemetry_target"></a>The `telemetry_target` block supports:

* `resources` -
  (Required)
  Lists references to the resources that are targeted by the policy.

<a name="nested_tracing_configuration"></a>The `tracing_configuration` block supports:

* `sampling_rate` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the tracing sampling rate.

* `custom_span_attributes` -
  (Optional)
  Provides key-value pairs for adding context to spans.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_tracing_configuration_custom_span_attributes).

* `parent_based_sampling` -
  (Optional)
  Configures honoring a sampled bit in downstream traceparentID headers.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_tracing_configuration_parent_based_sampling).


<a name="nested_tracing_configuration_custom_span_attributes"></a>The `custom_span_attributes` block supports:

* `attribute_name` -
  (Required)
  The attribute name.

* `literal_value` -
  (Optional)
  The literal value of the attribute.

* `from_header_value` -
  (Optional)
  The from header value of the attribute.

<a name="nested_tracing_configuration_parent_based_sampling"></a>The `parent_based_sampling` block supports:

* `enabled` -
  (Optional)
  Indicates whether parent based sampling is enabled.

* `sampling_rate` -
  (Optional)
  Specifies the sampling rate for parent based sampling.

<a name="nested_metrics_configuration"></a>The `metrics_configuration` block supports:

* `enabled` -
  (Required)
  Indicates whether metrics are enabled or disabled.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/telemetryPolicies/{{name}}`

* `create_time` -
  The timestamp when the resource was created.

* `update_time` -
  The timestamp when the resource was updated.

* `etag` -
  Etag of the resource.
  If this is provided, it must match the server's etag. If the provided etag
  does not match the server's etag, the request will fail with a 409 ABORTED
  error.

* `uid` -
  Specifies the server-assigned unique identifier for the policy.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 30 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 30 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 30 minutes.

## Import


TelemetryPolicy can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/telemetryPolicies/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{name}}`
* `{{location}}/{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import TelemetryPolicy using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-required value->"
    location = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_network_services_telemetry_policy.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import TelemetryPolicy using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/telemetryPolicies/{{name}}"
  to = google_network_services_telemetry_policy.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), TelemetryPolicy can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_network_services_telemetry_policy.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/telemetryPolicies/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_network_services_telemetry_policy.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_network_services_telemetry_policy.default {{location}}/{{name}}
```
